title: Two heads are better than one: current landscape of integrating QSP and machine learning — An ISoP QSP SIG white paper by the working group on the integration of quantitative systems pharmacology and machine learning

content.abstract_summary: ISoP QSP SIG white paper from a 21-member working group (18 academic/industry organizations) convened in September 2019 to identify opportunities for integrating QSP modeling and machine learning. Identifies four categories of current QSP+ML research activity, presents drug development case studies, and concludes that QSP+ML integration is in its early stages — moving from evaluating tools to building case studies — and serves as a foundation for future best-practices codification.
key_findings: Four integration categories identified: (1) ML applied to components of QSP models, (2) QSP used to generate training data for ML, (3) ML used to analyze QSP model outputs (sensitivity analysis, UQ), (4) hybrid QSP-ML architectures for mechanism + data-driven learning
Both QSP and ML are powerful individually; integration aims to overcome each approach's limitations — QSP's data hunger for parameterization vs. ML's lack of mechanistic interpretability
Multi-layer omics data (gene expression, proteomics, metabolomics, imaging) is the primary data source where ML adds value to QSP workflows
Working group concluded that the field was in early stages at time of writing (2019–2021 scoping): case study building phase, not yet best-practices codification
Rackauckas C (Pumas-AI / MIT) is listed as co-author — signals connection to Julia/Pumas-AI scientific ML ecosystem relevant to WG Pillar 1 (neural ODEs, SciML)
limitations: Scoped entirely within QSP (systems-scale mechanistic models) rather than pharmacometrics (NLME/compartmental PK/PD) — the MCS WG operates more in the PMx space, so direct overlap is partial
Published 2022 based on 2019–2021 work — landscape has shifted substantially with foundation models and SciML advances since then
Abstract-only read; four integration categories and case study details require full text to evaluate rigorously

extracted_claims.text: "Both approaches are powerful tools and there is considerable interest in integrating QSP modeling and ML. So far, a few successful implementations have been carried out from which we have learned about how each approach can overcome unique limitations of the other."
"The working group also concluded that the integration of QSP and ML is still in its early stages of moving from evaluating available technical tools to building case studies."

numerical_findings.description: Working group membership size at time of writing
numerical_findings.value: 21 members representing 18 academic and industry organizations

gaps_addressed: Provides the sister SIG (QSP) perspective on hybrid mechanistic-ML integration — directly relevant to differentiating MCS WG scope from QSP WG scope (QSP operates at network/systems scale; PMx at NLME/compartmental scale)

The four integration categories framework is a useful taxonomy for Pillar 1 scoping paper — MCS WG should reference this QSP categorization and clarify which categories apply to pharmacometrics vs. QSP contexts
Rackauckas (Julia SciML / neural ODEs) co-authorship signals that the Julia/SciML ecosystem is QSP-adjacent — MCS WG should be aware when evaluating tool recommendations
